before: Huang and Rust (2021) identify three types of AI: Mechanical, Thinking, and Feeling. Repetitive scanning of shelves falls mainly into the first type, the recognition of missing items and the recommendation of alternatives into the analytical processing. These features can be integrated into the same system. Just saying hello is not enough proof of emotional comprehension. A barcode scanner is an SST, not an AI. In this case intelligence is in interpreting shelf images and product requests; the payment interface is still the checkout. It is important not to overstate the benefits of AI and overlook the benefits of traditional automation.
after: Huang and Rust (2021) identify mechanical AI for repetitive tasks, thinking AI for analysis, and feeling AI for interpreting emotions. Shelf scanning mainly fits the first type; recognizing missing items and recommending alternatives require analysis. These features can be integrated into the same system. Just saying hello is not enough proof of emotional comprehension. A barcode scanner is self-service technology, not necessarily AI. In this case intelligence is in interpreting shelf images and product requests; the payment interface is still the checkout. We shouldn't overstate AI's benefits or overlook traditional automation.

before: Carrefour has also experimented with software tools in other countries in the UAE. In June 2023 it said it was introducing a feature called Hopla on its French website that gives shoppers ideas on how to buy food according to their budget and dietary requirements (Carrefour, 2023). In June 2021, Brazil's Nutri Choice announced an algorithm to compare nutritional scores and prices, based on purchase history (Carrefour, 2021). Both are non-committal as far as UAE deployments go. These examples provide information to our proposed optional planning assistant in stage 1 and product comparisons in stage 4. Recommendations should be based on local catalog information and should include a statement giving the rationale for the recommendations; nutritional ratings may not be used instead of checking the ingredients.

before: Wirtz et al. (2018) categorize service tasks into routine services and emotional and social judgment services. Their system enables automated periodic checks and still includes staff for disputes. These conceptual predictions are not local customer acceptance. Company publications also provide information on actions in lieu of independent satisfaction assessments. Prior to scaling up the proposed system, Carrefour UAE must first assess task performance and customer effort. Carrefour's examples go further than automation to conversational advice. In a bakery study, the recommendation effects were found to be different depending on the frequency of the visit (Song et al., 2024). It is a remotely controlled robot, which makes inferences about autonomous performance limited.

before: Even with assistive products, aisle signs and accessible routes continue to be crucial when entering a store and looking for products. This customer as co-producer approach is one of the reasons for the so-called "co-production" effect, which means that tasks may be outsourced to customers, but labor costs may be lowered due to the increased work required from customers (Wirtz, 2023). If it was more time-consuming to register, as an alternative, there would be a search screen. The second stage is thus made to maintain a route without the use of an application. The same journey should be facilitated through the physical servicescape and digital interface.
after: Even with digital tools, aisle signs and accessible routes continue to be crucial when entering a store and looking for products. The customer as co-producer approach explains how moving tasks to shoppers may lower labor costs while increasing customer work (Wirtz, 2023). A search screen helps if using it takes less time than asking an employee. Stage 2 therefore keeps a route without an app. The same journey should be facilitated through the physical servicescape and digital interface.

If a price is not given at F4, then the price should be checked and the basket saved to avoid restarting by the shopper.

If a discount is missing at F4, staff should check the price and save the basket so the shopper need not restart.

before: Once purchased, we would judge the retailer partially on how easily they are able to correct errors. If someone was to repeat the information to a chatbot and a staff member at F5, it would cause a lot of repetitive work. If the case record were forwarded to an authorized colleague, it would prevent the customer from having to re-enter the record. This is based on the principle for course process redesign proposed in the course, which emphasizes the elimination of steps in the process and the inclusion of recovery measures in case of self-service failure (Wirtz, 2023). We would seek assistance which was reliable during the interaction, particularly when there was something wrong.

before: Before implementing additional automation that reaches more customers, the store operations manager and inventory staff should test drive the stage 3 alert-to-restocking process. Apply a four week pilot with matched peak and off-peak periods after obtaining a baseline. Operating savings vs equipment, maintenance and training costs should be compared by the finance manager. Expansion should be at no increased cost or complaint, but as better availability. Determine how accurately alerts are made and how long it takes until a verified shelf correction, and how many shelves are available, compared to manual checking over similar trading times. Close the alert at F2 after staff have established that the shelf is safe. This failure-proofing control ensures that unfinished tasks do not lead to false promises of availability. Keep an eye on blocked aisles and staff workload; suspend robot operations following safety incident.
after: Before adding more customer-facing automation, the store operations manager and inventory staff should test drive the stage 3 alert-to-restocking process. Apply a four-week pilot with matched peak and off-peak periods after obtaining a baseline. Operating savings vs equipment, maintenance and training costs should be compared by the finance manager. Expansion should improve availability without increasing complaints or staff workload. Compare alert accuracy, time to verified shelf correction and product availability with manual checking over similar trading times. Close the alert at F2 only after staff confirm the item is available on the shelf. This failure-proofing control ensures that unfinished tasks do not lead to false promises of availability. Keep an eye on blocked aisles and staff workload; suspend robot operations following a safety incident.

before: The checkout supervisor and the customer service manager should be co-owners of fail points F4 and F5. Have all item, price and receipt information in one place, include customer verification before making changes, and empower employees within a predetermined refund policy. Acknowledgment within 2 minutes after an in-store help request is made, and a human response within 1 working day of a post purchase case is proposed as pilot standards. Monitor the percentage of contacts that meet the standards, those that repeat and the amount of time that is taken to resolve the contacts these are targets and not measured outcomes.

Monitor the percentage meeting these standards, repeat contacts and total resolution time. These are targets, not measured outcomes.
